text: でもよ。
translation: But, you know.
grammar: でもよ is a colloquial sentence fragment — Wakka trails off, implying unspoken disagreement or hesitation. The よ softens but also signals he has something to say.

text: せっかくだから優勝してよな! / オウ!
translation: Since you've come this far, go win it all! / Yeah!

vocabulary.meaning: since you have the chance, taking the trouble to

grammar: せっかくだから means 'since we've gone to this trouble / since we have this opportunity.' The て-form + よな combination is a friendly imperative seeking buy-in.

text: オレベンチっすか?
translation: Am I on the bench?

vocabulary.meaning: casual copula (contracted form of です)

grammar: オレベンチっすか is informal: オレ (I) + ベンチ (bench) + っすか (casual question form of ですか). The speaker drops the topic particle は.

text: ベンチは俺だ。 / 決勝戦は、こいつに任せる。
translation: I'll be on the bench. / I'm leaving the final to this guy.

vocabulary.meaning: to entrust, to leave to someone

text: ここまで来たら絶対に優勝だ! / ルカゴワーズをぶっ飛ばす!
translation: Now that we've come this far, we're definitely winning! / We're gonna blast the Luca Goers away!

vocabulary.meaning: to blow away, to thrash, to knock out (colloquial)

grammar: ここまで来たら is a conditional 'now that we've come this far.' ぶっ飛ばす combines the intensifying prefix ぶっ with 飛ばす (to fly/send flying), meaning to devastate.

text: 行くぞ! / オン!
translation: Let's go! / Yeah!

text: 気絶してるとこ、見ちゃった。
translation: I saw you passed out.

vocabulary.meaning: the moment/state of doing ~ (ところ contracted)
ended up doing ~ (contraction of てしまった, often with slight regret)

grammar: 見ちゃった = 見てしまった — the ちゃう form expresses that the seeing happened unintentionally or unexpectedly. とこ is a colloquial contraction of ところ ('the place/moment where').

text: ち、かっこつけどころだったのにな。
translation: Tch, that was supposed to be my moment to look cool.

vocabulary.meaning: to act cool, to show off, to put on airs

grammar: かっこつけどころ = the moment to look cool. のにな at the end expresses frustrated disappointment — 'it was supposed to be that but it wasn't.'

text: あんたは、あれでいいんだよね?
translation: You're okay with that, right?
grammar: いいんだよね combines いい (good/okay) + んだ (explanatory) + よね (seeking confirmation). The speaker is checking that Tidus is fine with how things went.

text: リサイドオラカの合言葉! / 優勝だ!
translation: The Besaid Aurochs' rally cry! / Victory!

text: 若さんのために! / オー!
translation: For the young man! / Yeah!

vocabulary.meaning: young (person); here used as a nickname/title)

grammar: 若さん is an affectionate way to address Tidus as 'the young one.' のために here expresses dedication.

text: さあ、いよいよクライマックス! / まもなく、もうまもなく決勝戦がスタートです
translation: Now, it's finally the climax! / Very soon, the final match will start any moment now.

vocabulary.meaning: finally, at last, more and more

text: それにしても一体誰が / 誰がこの組み合わせを予想したでしょうか
translation: Even so, who on earth — who could have predicted this matchup?

vocabulary.meaning: on earth, in the world (intensifier with questions)

grammar: 〜でしょうか is a rhetorical question form — the commentator is expressing amazement rather than genuinely asking.

text: 上昇ルカグワーズと決勝戦で対決するのは
translation: Facing the rising Luca Goers in the final is…
grammar: This is a suspended clause — the sentence is left incomplete, creating suspense before naming the opposing team.

text: 万年初戦敗退チームビサイドオーラが
translation: …the perennial first-round losers, the Besaid Aurochs!

vocabulary.meaning: defeat and elimination, being knocked out

grammar: 万年初戦敗退 is a compound modifier: 'the team that perennially loses in the first round.' The が here is a subject marker continuing from the previous sentence.

text: まさに驚異の大盤クロアスですね
translation: Truly a miraculous giant upset, isn't it!
grammar: 大盤クロアス appears to be the commentator's portmanteau/nickname for a major upset (大番狂わせ context). ですね seeks agreement.

text: ДИНАМИЧНАЯ МУЗЫКА / おーっと!早くもこぜり合いだ!
translation: [DYNAMIC MUSIC] / Oh! Already a scuffle!

text: オーラか完全に舐められています!
translation: The Aurochs are being completely underestimated!

vocabulary.meaning: to lick; to underestimate, to look down on (colloquial)

grammar: 舐められています is the passive form of 舐める in its figurative sense: 'to be looked down upon / underestimated.' The passive + います indicates an ongoing state.

text: ここで前半終了です! / いやー、ゴーアンズ強い!
translation: And that's the end of the first half! / Wow, the Goers are strong!

text: 全くもって強い!
translation: Absolutely, completely strong!
grammar: 全くもって is an emphatic intensifier — stronger than 全く alone. The commentator is gushing about the Goers' dominance.

text: Субтитры создавал DimaTorzok
translation: [Russian subtitle credit: subtitles created by DimaTorzok]

text: しびれを切らしたサポーターたちのコールがますます大きくなってきました
translation: The chants of the impatient supporters are growing louder and louder.

vocabulary.meaning: to lose patience, to get fed up waiting

grammar: 大きくなってきました uses the て+くる construction to indicate a change gradually approaching the present moment — getting louder over time leading up to now.

text: 大らかの選手たちは戦意喪失気味です
translation: The Aurochs players seem to be losing their fighting spirit.

vocabulary.meaning: tending toward ~, somewhat ~, a touch of ~

grammar: 〜気味 (ぎみ) attaches to nouns or verb stems to mean 'somewhat' or 'showing signs of.' 戦意喪失気味 = 'showing signs of losing their fighting spirit.'

text: このまま大会から消えていくのか
translation: Are they going to fade out of the tournament just like this?

vocabulary.meaning: just like this, as things stand
to disappear, to vanish, to fade away

grammar: 消えていく uses て+いく to express movement/change away from the present — fading out, disappearing into the distance (here, eliminated from the tournament).

text: スタジアム全体が / 我れんばかりの輪っかコールです
translation: The entire stadium is filled with a deafening Wakka chant.

vocabulary.meaning: as if about to burst/split, deafening (lit. 'as if it would crack')

grammar: 割れんばかり is a literary expression: ばかり here means 'to the extent that it seems about to ~.' 割れんばかりのコール = chants so loud the stadium seems about to crack.

text: ああっと / あの選手はどうしたのでしょう
translation: Oh! What has that player done?
grammar: 〜のでしょう is a polite speculative question — the commentator is wondering aloud about the player's unexpected action.

text: 試合を放棄したのでしょうか / スフィアプールを出ていきます
translation: Has he abandoned the match? / He is leaving the sphere pool.

vocabulary.meaning: to abandon, to give up, to forfeit

text: そりゃちょっとは寂しかったさ
translation: Well, it was a little lonely, yeah.

vocabulary.meaning: of course, naturally (contraction of それは)
at least a little, to some extent

grammar: さ at the end is a masculine sentence-final particle expressing a casual concession — 'yeah, I'll admit it.'

text: でもあれはワッカとビサイドオーラカの大切な試合だったからな
translation: But that was Wakka and the Besaid Aurochs' important match, so.
grammar: からな at the end of a sentence gives a casual explanatory reason — 'because [that's how it was].' The trailing な softens the statement.

text: んーどうしたんでしょう / 場内が湧いています
translation: Hmm, what's happening? / The arena is erupting!

vocabulary.meaning: inside the venue, within the arena
to well up; to erupt (with excitement), to go wild

grammar: 湧いています describes the crowd going wild — 湧く in this context means to bubble up with excitement.

text: あーっとワッカ選手です / 元気に復帰してきました
translation: Oh! It's player Wakka! / He's come back, full of energy!

vocabulary.meaning: to return, to come back, to rejoin

grammar: 復帰してきました uses て+くる to indicate movement back toward the speaker/scene — returning to the pool.

text: チームメイトが温かく迎えます
translation: His teammates welcome him warmly.

vocabulary.meaning: to welcome, to greet, to receive

text: 試合には負けましたが / 今年のオーラ化はなかなかの健闘を見せました
translation: They lost the match, but this year's Aurochs put up quite a fight.

vocabulary.meaning: hard fighting, valiant effort, good show

grammar: 健闘を見せました = 'showed a valiant effort.' なかなか here is used as a positive intensifier — 'quite/remarkably.'

text: Субтитры создавал DimaTorzok
translation: [Russian subtitle credit: subtitles created by DimaTorzok]

text: 何が始まったの?
translation: What's started?
grammar: の at the end makes this a soft question (feminine/casual speech style), softening what would otherwise be the blunter 何が始まったか.

text: なんだよこれ
translation: What the heck is this?
grammar: なんだよこれ is a colloquial exclamation of surprise or frustration — なんだ (what is) + よ (assertive particle) + これ (this). Word order reversed for emphasis.

text: 本当に出発しちゃうんすか?
translation: Are you really going to leave already?

vocabulary.meaning: to go ahead and do ~ (contraction of てしまう)
is it that ~? (casual question, contraction of んですか)

grammar: 出発しちゃうんすか combines 出発する + ちゃう (てしまう) + んすか (explanatory question). The ちゃう adds a sense of 'really going ahead and doing it?'

text: ゆっくり休んだ方がいいっすよ / ユーナの旅は先を急ぐ
translation: You should take it easy and rest / Yuna's journey doesn't have time to spare.

vocabulary.meaning: it would be better to ~, you should ~
to press on ahead, to hurry forward

grammar: 〜た方がいい is a standard recommendation structure. 先を急ぐ is an idiomatic phrase meaning 'to be in a hurry to get ahead.'

text: 休んでるわけにはいかねえんだよ
translation: I can't afford to be resting.

vocabulary.meaning: cannot afford to, must not, it won't do to ~
can't go (rough masculine contraction of いかない)

grammar: 〜わけにはいかない expresses that something is socially/morally/practically impossible to do. いかねえ is a rough colloquial form of いかない (Wakka's speech style).

text: こら!シャキッとしろお前ら
translation: Hey! Shape up, you guys!

vocabulary.meaning: to shape up, to snap to attention, to get it together

grammar: 〜しろ is the imperative form. シャキッと is an onomatopoeic adverb suggesting sharpness and alertness.

text: ブリッツのシーズンは始まったばっかだろうが / そのしけた面はなんだ
translation: The blitzball season has only just started! / What's with those gloomy faces?
grammar: ばっか is a colloquial contraction of ばかり (just/only). だろうが adds emphasis and a slightly confrontational tone. しけた面 is informal — しける means to look glum.

text: じゃあな / 元気でやるよ
translation: See ya. / I'll be doing well.

text: 元気でな
translation: Take care.

text: 声が小さい
translation: Your voices are too small.
grammar: A terse, blunt criticism — Wakka complaining the team's farewell was too half-hearted.

text: もういいの? / ああいうのは弱いからな / 俺、待たせたな、ユーナ。
translation: Is that it? / That sort of thing is my weakness, you know. / I kept you waiting, Yuna.

vocabulary.meaning: weak; here: weak spot, soft spot

grammar: 待たせたな is a causative past form — 'I caused [you] to wait.' The な softens it into a gentle apology.

text: モヤモヤに蹴りつけてきた。
translation: I kicked away all those murky feelings.

vocabulary.meaning: murky feeling, lingering doubt, unsettled emotion
to kick hard at, to kick away

grammar: 〜てきた here indicates completed action that was done and brought back to the present state — he resolved his emotional baggage and has now returned.

text: これからはユーナのガード一筋だ。
translation: From now on, I'm devoted solely to being Yuna's guardian.

vocabulary.meaning: from now on, from here on
single-minded devotion, solely focused on one thing

grammar: 〜一筋 means complete, single-minded dedication to one thing — a strong pledge of commitment.

text: じゃあ、ワッカさん、改めてよろしくお願いします。
translation: Well then, Wakka, once again, I'm in your care.

vocabulary.word: よろしくお願いします
vocabulary.reading: よろしくおねがいします
vocabulary.meaning: please take care of me, I look forward to working with you

grammar: 改めて signals a fresh, formal start — Yuna is marking the official recommencement of their journey.

text: こちらこそ。何卒よろしくお願いいたします、と。
translation: Likewise. Please take good care of me as well — there.

vocabulary.meaning: it is I who should say so, likewise
humble form of します (to do)

grammar: と at the very end is a trailing quotation marker — Wakka is quoting himself being formal, with a self-aware 'there, I said it' nuance (slightly joking).

text: で、あの魔物どもなんだったか分かったか? / 全然。魔物がどこから入り込んだのか不明。 / シーモアローシの活躍で、マイカソウロウシはご無事。
translation: So, did you find out what those monsters were? / Not at all. It's unknown where the monsters got in from. / Thanks to Seymour's efforts, Grand Maester Mika is safe.

vocabulary.meaning: to get in, to sneak in, to infiltrate

grammar: どもis a plural suffix with slightly contemptuous nuance (those monsters). 〜のか adds an explanatory/question nuance to the clause.

text: 情報はそれくらいね。 / シーモアローシの召喚獣、すごかったな。
translation: That's about all the information we have. / Seymour's aeon was amazing, wasn't it.

vocabulary.meaning: about that much, that's the extent of it

grammar: すごかったな is past tense + な — a masculine reflective remark ('that was amazing, wasn't it').

text: わかってんのかよ!
translation: Do you even understand?!
grammar: わかってんのかよ = わかっているのか + よ. The contracted form with のかよ expresses exasperation and challenge — 'do you even get it?!'

text: 全部あんたのせいなんだ! / 真に飲み込まれたのも、スフィアに放り出されたのも、ザラルカードに変えられるのも、全部すべて瓶だ!
translation: It's all your fault! / Being swallowed by Sin, being thrown into the Sphere, being turned into Spira — all of it, every bit of it, is you!

vocabulary.meaning: to throw out, to toss out

grammar: 〜のも〜のも〜のも is a 'not just X but also Y and Z' listing pattern. Each のも marks a parallel item in Tidus's accusation.

text: 何もかもあんたのせいだ!
translation: Everything is your fault!
grammar: 何もかも is a more emphatic way of saying 全部 — 'absolutely everything without exception.'

text: あんた、何者なんだ?
translation: Just who are you?

vocabulary.meaning: who, what kind of person, what entity

grammar: 何者 is more intense than 誰 — it implies 'what kind of being are you?' suggesting mystery or suspicion.

text: 親父のこと知ってんだよな?
translation: You know about my old man, right?

vocabulary.meaning: you know, don't you (contracted: 知っているのだよな)

grammar: 知ってんだよな = 知っているのだよな — the んだ adds explanatory nuance while よな seeks confirmation. Tidus is pressing Auron.

text: ユーナの親父さんとも知り合いなんだろ? / そうだな
translation: You're also acquainted with Yuna's father, right? / That's right.

text: どういうことだよ! / おかしいだろ! / 何もおかしいことはない
translation: What does that mean?! / That's weird, isn't it! / There's nothing strange about it.

vocabulary.meaning: what does that mean, what's going on

grammar: だよ adds forceful assertion. だろ at the end of おかしいだろ seeks agreement — 'it IS weird, right?' Auron's flat denial 何もおかしいことはない uses the pattern 何も〜ない (nothing ~).

text: ジェクト、ブラスカ、そして俺
translation: Jecht, Braska, and me.
grammar: A terse, deliberate listing — Auron naming the three members of Braska's pilgrimage ten years ago.

text: 三人でシンを倒したのが10年前 / 後に俺だけがザナルカンドへ渡り
translation: The three of us defeated Sin ten years ago. / Afterward, only I crossed over to Zanarkand,

vocabulary.meaning: together as three people, the three of us
to cross over, to go across

grammar: 〜のが10年前 is a nominalized clause: 'the thing of [us] defeating Sin was ten years ago.' 後に is a formal time adverb.

text: お前の成長を見守っていた / いつの日か、お前をスピラに連れて行くために
translation: And watched over your growth — in order to one day bring you to Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: to watch over, to keep an eye on
to take (someone) with one, to bring

grammar: 〜ために at the end marks purpose: 'in order to.' 見守っていた is the progressive past — he was continuously watching over Tidus throughout.

text: どうして俺なんだよ!
translation: Why me?!
grammar: 俺なんだよ — なんだ is the explanatory copula; combined with どうして and the exclamatory よ, the sentence is a frustrated, demanding 'Why on earth me?!'

text: ジェクトの頼みでな
translation: It was Jecht's request.
grammar: でな is a casual explanatory ending — 〜で (by means of, because of) + な (softening male sentence-final particle).

text: 親父生きてるのか
translation: Is my old man alive?
grammar: 〜てるのか = 〜ているのか — a direct, raw question with のか marking surprise and genuine uncertainty.

text: あの状態を生きていると言えるなら
translation: If you can call that state living…

vocabulary.meaning: can be called ~, can be said to be ~

grammar: The conditional 〜なら here implies a doubtful concession: 'IF one can even call it that…' The sentence is left grammatically open, creating an ominous trailing-off.

text: あいつはもう人の姿をしていない
translation: He no longer has the form of a human.

vocabulary.meaning: human form, the appearance of a person

grammar: 姿をしていない = does not have the form/appearance of. 〜をしている indicates possessing a certain appearance/state.

text: だがあれの片隅には確実にジェクトの意識が残っている
translation: But in a corner of that being, Jecht's consciousness certainly remains.

text: あれに接触した時
translation: When you made contact with that thing,

vocabulary.meaning: to make contact, to come into contact with

grammar: This sentence is suspended — it sets up a conditional/temporal clause that continues in the next line.

text: お前もジェクトを感じたはずだ
translation: You must have felt Jecht too.

vocabulary.meaning: should be, ought to be, must be (logical expectation)

grammar: 〜はずだ expresses logical certainty based on reasoning — Auron is certain Tidus sensed Jecht because of what happened.

text: まさか…
translation: No way…

vocabulary.meaning: no way, surely not, that can't be

grammar: まさか alone, trailed by ellipsis, expresses disbelief or dawning horrified realization.

text: そうだ
translation: That's right.

text: シンはジェクトだ
translation: Sin is Jecht.
grammar: The blunt declarative with だ — one of the game's major revelations, delivered with maximum brevity.

text: グッダレ!なんだよそれ!
translation: Goddammit! What the hell is that?!

vocabulary.meaning: what the hell is that (frustrated exclamation)

grammar: グッダレ is Tidus's anglicized exclamation. なんだよそれ = それ (that) + なんだよ (what is it, forcefully) — word order inverted for emotional punch.

text: 真実を見せてやる / 怒るのもなくのもそれからにしろ
translation: I will show you the truth. / Save your anger and your tears for after.
grammar: 〜のも〜のも is a parallel listing: 'both X and Y.' にしろ is an imperative form of にする — 'make it after that / leave it until after.'

text: 俺についてこい
translation: Follow me.
grammar: ついてこい is the imperative form of ついてくる — a blunt, authoritative command.

text: 嫌だと言ったら / お前の物語は終わらない
translation: If you say no — your story will never end.

vocabulary.meaning: no, I don't want to, I refuse

grammar: 〜と言ったら sets up a conditional: 'if you say ~.' The negative 終わらない in this context means Tidus's journey/purpose will remain incomplete — a heavy, philosophical threat.

text: それがどうしたってんだ
translation: So what about it?

vocabulary.meaning: so what, what about it (defiant dismissal)

grammar: どうしたってんだ is a rough contraction of どうしたというんだ — 'and what of it?' Tidus's defiant bluff.

text: そうか / ならば仕方あるまい
translation: I see. / Then there's nothing to be done.

vocabulary.meaning: if that is the case, then (formal conditional)
there's no helping it (literary/formal: まい = volitional negative)

grammar: 仕方あるまい is a formal/literary expression — まい is a classical volitional negative auxiliary meaning 'will not' or 'there is no ~.' More formal than 仕方ない.

text: 好きにしろ / 来るか来ないか選ぶのはお前だ
translation: Do as you like. / Whether you come or not — the choice is yours.
grammar: 来るか来ないか is a か〜か structure — 'whether X or not X.' 選ぶのはお前だ = 'the one who chooses is you' (の nominalizer + は topic + お前 subject).

text: 馬鹿にしながって 好きにしろとか言ってさ
translation: Making fun of me and saying things like 'do as you like'…

vocabulary.meaning: to make fun of, to look down on, to ridicule

grammar: ながって is a contracted form of ながら + って (quotation/complaint marker). This is Tidus grumbling to himself about Auron's attitude.

text: 選ぶのは俺だとか言ってさ / だけど俺にはどうしようもないんだっての
translation: 'The choice is yours' he says — but I really have no choice in the matter.

vocabulary.meaning: there's nothing one can do, helpless, no way out
I'm telling you it's ~ (emphatic, slightly exasperated)

grammar: どうしようもない = 'there's no way/nothing I can do.' んだっての is a colloquial emphatic expression, like 'I'm telling you!' — expressing frustrated resignation.

text: あんたに言われた通りにするしかないんだ
translation: I have no choice but to do exactly as you say.

vocabulary.meaning: have no choice but to ~, can only ~

grammar: 〜しかない is a strong constraint pattern: 'the only option is ~.' 言われた通りに = following instructions exactly.

text: 不満だろうな
translation: You must be dissatisfied.
grammar: だろうな is a soft, reflective conjecture — Auron acknowledging Tidus's feelings with mild empathy.

text: それとも不安か?
translation: Or are you anxious?

text: それでいい
translation: That's fine.

vocabulary.meaning: that's fine, that's good enough, that will do

grammar: A calm, somewhat cryptic approval — Auron telling Tidus that his uncertainty is appropriate.

text: ザナルカンは帰れるのかな
translation: I wonder if I can return to Zanarkand.

vocabulary.meaning: I wonder if ~, I'm not sure if ~

grammar: 〜のかな is a soft, introspective wondering — less confident than だろうか, more personal and doubtful.

text: オジェクト次第だな
translation: It depends on Jecht.

vocabulary.meaning: depending on, up to, subject to

grammar: 〜次第だ means 'it depends on ~' — whatever happens is contingent on the named factor.

text: 俺はユーナのガードになる
translation: I'll become Yuna's guardian.

text: お前もついてくれ
translation: You come along too.
grammar: 〜てくれ is a direct, masculine request — Tidus asking Auron to join them.

text: あいつここに残るのかな / アーロンさんと知り合いなんでしょ
translation: Is he staying here? / He's acquainted with Auron, right?
grammar: 〜のかな — soft wondering. 〜なんでしょ is a casual confirmation-seeking tag, slightly softer than 〜ですよね.

text: 確かに知り合いと会えたわね / でも、ザナルカンドに帰れるのかな?
translation: It's true he got to meet an acquaintance. / But I wonder if he can return to Zanarkand?
grammar: わね is a characteristically feminine sentence-final particle. 〜のかな is the gentle wondering form.

text: どっちにしても寂しくなるな
translation: Either way it'll get lonely.
grammar: なるな — なる (to become) + な (male reflective particle). The sentence expresses resigned melancholy.

text: まだ、街にいるよね? / 私、挨拶してこようかな
translation: He's still in town, right? / Maybe I'll go say goodbye.

vocabulary.meaning: maybe I'll go do ~ and come back

grammar: 〜てこようかな = 〜てくる + volitional + かな. The てくる indicates doing something and returning; かな is soft self-directed wondering.

text: あっ! / おお! / アーロンさんも?
translation: Oh! / Wow! / Auron too?
grammar: Short exclamations of surprise as Auron appears to join the party.

text: ユーナ
translation: Yuna.

text: 今この時より、お前のガードを務めたい / えっ?
translation: From this moment on, I wish to serve as your guardian. / Huh?

vocabulary.meaning: to serve as, to perform the role of, to act as

grammar: 〜より indicates a starting point (from). 務めたい = want to serve. The phrasing is deliberately formal and solemn.

text: マジですか? / 不都合か? / いいえ
translation: Seriously? / Is it inconvenient? / No.
grammar: マジですか is casual; Auron's 不都合か is clipped and formal. The contrast in register reflects their characters.

text: ね、みんないいよね? / あ、あったりまいっす!
translation: Right? Everyone's okay with it, right? / Of — of course!

vocabulary.meaning: of course, naturally (colloquial form of 当たり前)

grammar: ね〜よね is a double confirmation-seeking pattern. あったりまい is a casual/emphatic contraction of 当たり前.

text: 文句なんかあるわけないっす!
translation: There's no way there'd be any complaints!

vocabulary.meaning: there's no way there is ~, it's impossible that there is ~

grammar: 〜わけない (わけがない) = 'there's no way.' なんか adds a dismissive nuance — 'complaints of all things.'

text: ジェクトさんはお元気なんですか?
translation: Is Jecht doing well?
grammar: お元気なんですか — なんですか adds a nuance of seeking explanation or clarification, not just a plain yes/no.

text: 知らん / 10年前にお別れときだ
translation: I don't know. / We parted ways ten years ago.
grammar: 知らん is a rough/blunt form of 知らない — stereotypically used by brusque older male characters. お別れときだ appears to be 別れ時 (time of parting).

text: そうですか
translation: I see.

text: そのうち会えるさ
translation: You'll get to meet him eventually.
grammar: さ at the end gives a light, somewhat casual reassurance — Auron's rare moment of something like warmth.

text: 楽しみにしてます
translation: I'm looking forward to it.
grammar: 〜にしています = ongoing state of looking forward to. A poignant irony given what 'meeting Jecht' will entail.

text: 見て見て
translation: Look, look!
grammar: Reduplication of the imperative 見て for emphasis and childlike excitement.

text: そんだけ吹ければ上出来だな
translation: If you can whistle that well, that's pretty good.

vocabulary.meaning: that much, to that extent (casual: それだけ)
well done, above expectations, excellent result

grammar: そんだけ = それだけ (casual contraction). 〜ければ is the conditional of い-adjectives and some verbs — 'if [you] can ~.' 上出来 is an approving remark.

text: 元気ないね / かもな
translation: You don't seem very energetic. / Maybe so.

vocabulary.meaning: maybe, perhaps (casual: かもしれないな)

grammar: かもな = かもしれな(い) + な — a casual, slightly resigned acknowledgment.

text: 叫ぶ?
translation: Want to shout?

vocabulary.meaning: to shout, to cry out, to scream

grammar: A direct, simple offer — Yuna suggesting they shout to feel better. The ? makes it a question without any extra verb.

text: そういうのとはちょっと違うかな
translation: That's a little different from what I need, I think.
grammar: とは marks contrast — 'as opposed to that.' かな at the end softens the polite refusal.

text: あのさ
translation: Hey, you know…
grammar: あのさ is a soft, attention-getting opener — Yuna is about to say something meaningful.

text: 自分で言うのも変だけど / 召喚師とガードっていうのはスピラの希望の光なんだよね
translation: It's weird to say it myself, but — summoners and guardians are the light of hope for Spira, you know.
grammar: 自分で言うのも変だけど is a self-deprecating opener: 'it's strange to say it myself but~.' 〜っていうのは is the colloquial topic-introducing form of というのは.

text: いろんな人が私たちに注目してる
translation: All kinds of people are watching us.

vocabulary.meaning: various, all kinds of (colloquial: いろいろな)
to pay attention to, to watch, to focus on

grammar: 〜ている marks ongoing state — people are constantly watching them.

text: だから落ち込んでるところとか
translation: So, times when I'm down, or…

vocabulary.meaning: to feel down, to be depressed, to sink low
the state of doing ~, a moment of ~
and so on, things like (listing with implication of more)

grammar: とか after ところ lists examples with a trailing implication — 'things like being down, or [other weak moments].' The sentence continues in the next line.

text: 元気ないところとか
translation: Or moments when I have no energy,
grammar: Parallel structure continuing from the previous line — another とか item in the list.

text: 見せたくないんだ
translation: I don't want to show that.
grammar: 見せたくないんだ = 見せたくない + んだ. The んだ conveys that this is an earnest personal explanation, not just a statement.

text: わかる気がする
translation: I think I understand.

vocabulary.meaning: to feel like, to have a feeling that

grammar: 〜気がする expresses a feeling or intuition rather than certainty — 'I have a feeling I understand / it feels like I get it.'

text: はいじゃあ笑顔の練習
translation: Okay then, smile practice!
grammar: A bright, directive announcement — Yuna pivoting to action with cheerful determination.

text: なんだか変だぞこの練習 / 次、声出してみよう
translation: This practice feels kind of weird. / Next, let's try making some sound.

vocabulary.meaning: to make a sound, to raise one's voice

grammar: 〜てみよう is the volitional of 〜てみる — 'let's try doing ~.' An invitation to attempt something.

text: はい、やってみて
translation: Okay, give it a try.

vocabulary.meaning: to try doing, to give it a go

grammar: やってみて is the て-form of やってみる used as a soft imperative — 'please try doing it.'

text: 这 / そこまでやらなくても…
translation: [Chinese character / subtitle artifact] / You didn't have to go that far…

vocabulary.meaning: even without doing ~, don't have to ~

grammar: 〜なくてもいい (implied) = 'you didn't need to do that.' The trailing ellipsis shows bemused trailing off.

text: おかしい / ユーラのせいだろ
translation: This is ridiculous. / It's Yuna's fault, right.
grammar: だろ is a casual confirmation-seeking tag: 'right?' Tidus is laughing and blaming Yuna for the absurd situation.

text: ありがとう
translation: Thank you.

text: 笑いながら旅したいんだ
translation: I want to travel while laughing.

vocabulary.meaning: while doing ~, at the same time as ~

grammar: 〜ながら here means doing two things simultaneously. したいんだ = want to do + explanatory んだ. Yuna's key line expressing her philosophy.

text: もし、ダメそうな時は、指笛拭いて。
translation: If it seems like I'm not doing well, blow your finger whistle.

vocabulary.meaning: seems bad, looks like it won't work

grammar: 〜そう attached to an adjective/verb means 'seems like ~.' もし〜時は is a soft conditional: 'if/when ~.'

text: そしたら私、飛んでいく。
translation: Then I'll come flying to you.

vocabulary.meaning: if/when that happens, then (casual: そうしたら)
to fly off, to come flying

grammar: 飛んでいく uses て+いく: movement away from the current position — flying toward Tidus. A tender, iconic promise.

text: うん。
translation: Yeah.

text: じゃ、行こっか。
translation: Well then, shall we go?

vocabulary.meaning: shall we go? (casual volitional: 行こうか contracted)

grammar: 行こっか = 行こうか (volitional + か for soft suggestion). The contraction and っ give it a light, cheerful quality.

text: 何見てんだよ!
translation: What are you looking at?!

vocabulary.meaning: what are you looking at (contracted: 見ているんだよ)

grammar: 見てんだよ = 見ているんだよ — contracted casual speech. だよ adds an accusatory or confrontational edge. Tidus catching others watching their private moment.

text: お前たち変になったかと心配してたんじゃねえか / 大丈夫!
translation: We were worried you two had gone weird! / We're fine!

vocabulary.meaning: to go strange, to become weird

grammar: 〜てたんじゃねえか = 〜ていたのではないか — a rough colloquial way of saying 'weren't we?' (confirmation of the past). じゃねえか = じゃないか in rough speech.

text: それでは召喚師ユーナ、これよりジョジェジーン目指して出発です
translation: Well then, summoner Yuna — we hereby depart for Djose!

vocabulary.meaning: to aim for, to head toward

grammar: これより is a formal way to say 'from this point.' 〜目指して = heading toward ~, aiming for ~.

text: ガードの皆さん、よろしくお願いします
translation: Guardians, I am counting on you all.

vocabulary.word: よろしくお願いします
vocabulary.reading: よろしくおねがいします
vocabulary.meaning: I ask for your favor, please take care of me

text: 召喚師様
translation: My Lady Summoner.
grammar: 様 is the most respectful honorific suffix — the child is addressing Yuna with deep reverence.

text: 召喚師様なの? / うん、ユーナっていうの / ヒクリ
translation: Are you really a summoner? / Yes, my name is Yuna. / Hikari.

vocabulary.meaning: my name is ~, I'm called ~ (casual self-introduction)

grammar: なの as a question is characteristic of children's speech and feminine register. っていうの is a casual way to give one's name (lit. 'I'm called ~').

text: こんにちは、ヒクリ
translation: Hello, Hikari.

text: ユーナ様、凪説作ってくれる?
translation: Lady Yuna, will you make a Calm for us?

vocabulary.meaning: the Calm (period of peace after Sin is defeated)
to make, to create, to bring about

grammar: 〜てくれる is a request form — 'will you do ~ for me?' The child is asking Yuna to create the Calm.

text: はーい、楽しみに待っててね
translation: Yes! Look forward to it, okay?

vocabulary.meaning: to wait with anticipation, to look forward to waiting
please keep doing ~ (contracted: ていてね)

grammar: 待っててね = 待っていてね — a gentle request to keep waiting. The はーい is a drawn-out, warm affirmation.

text: やったー!
translation: Yay!

vocabulary.meaning: I did it! Yay! (exclamation of joy)

text: ユーナ様の凪説、楽しみに待たせていただきますね
translation: I shall look forward to Lady Yuna's Calm with great anticipation.
grammar: 〜させていただく is a highly humble expression: literally 'allow me to wait.' The parent/adult is using very polite language in contrast to the child's simpler speech.

text: はい、頑張ります
translation: Yes, I will do my best.

vocabulary.meaning: to do one's best, to work hard, to persevere

text: ガードの皆様もご苦労様です
translation: And thank you for your hard work, guardians.

vocabulary.meaning: thank you for your hard work (said to people of equal/lower status)

grammar: ご苦労様 acknowledges someone's effort. Note: 〜です here makes it more neutral/polite.

text: 凪説って何?
translation: What's the Calm?

vocabulary.meaning: what is ~? (casual inquiry about a term)

grammar: 〜って is a casual quotation/topic marker — 'speaking of X, what is it?' Tidus asking about game-world lore.

text: 凪説はシンがいない期間のこと。召喚師がシンを倒してから、次のシンが現れるまでの期間。
translation: The Calm is the period when Sin is absent. The period from when a summoner defeats Sin until the next Sin appears.
grammar: 〜てから〜まで is a standard temporal construction: 'from after doing X until Y.' の期間 = 'the period of.'

text: ああ、あれ?
translation: Oh — wait, then?
grammar: ああ marks dawning realization; あれ is a filler/pause sound expressing 'hmm, but then~' — Tidus working something out.

text: シンは生まれ変わるの。
translation: Sin is reborn.

vocabulary.meaning: to be reborn, to be reincarnated

grammar: の at the end (feminine/explanatory) — Yuna explaining an important fact with gentle emphasis.

text: そうか!変だと思ってたんだよな。ユーナの親父さんが10年前にシンを倒したんだろ?それなのにまだシンがいるのはどういうわけだってさ。
translation: Oh I see! I thought it was strange. Yuna's father defeated Sin ten years ago, right? And yet Sin still exists — I was wondering what that was about.

vocabulary.meaning: and yet, even so, despite that

grammar: 〜んだよな expresses self-reflection on a past state of mind. それなのに is a concessive: 'and yet despite that.' どういうわけだってさ is a casual report of his past wondering.

text: でもさ、シンが生まれ変わるのを知ってて
translation: But even knowing that Sin is reborn,
grammar: 〜のを知っていて — knowing that [fact] but ~ (concessive). The sentence is suspended to build into the next line's request.

text: それでもシンを倒すのは無駄 / なんて言わないでね
translation: Even so, defeating Sin is pointless — don't say things like that, okay?
grammar: なんて言わないでね = 'please don't say things like that.' なんて quotes and dismisses the concept of 'it's pointless.'

text: たとえどんなに短くても / シンに怯えることなく
translation: No matter how short it may be / without fearing Sin,

vocabulary.meaning: to be frightened, to cower, to tremble in fear

grammar: たとえ〜ても is a concessive: 'even if / no matter how.' ことなく is a literary negative: 'without doing ~.'

text: 安心して眠れる日々 / 何者にも変えられない
translation: Days in which you can sleep peacefully — irreplaceable by anything.

vocabulary.meaning: to feel at ease, to be relieved, to be at peace

grammar: 何者にも〜ない is a total negative scope: 'not by anything/anyone.' 変えられない is the potential negative passive — 'cannot be replaced.'

text: 大切な時間を生み出すこと / それを無駄だなんて言わないで
translation: Creating precious time — don't call that futile.

vocabulary.meaning: to create, to produce, to give birth to

grammar: Yuna's philosophical key speech. 生み出すこと = the act of creating (こと nominalizes the verb). それを無駄だなんて = 'calling that futile' (なんて quotes and rejects the label).

text: あの時のユーナの言葉 / よく覚えてるよ
translation: Yuna's words from that moment — I remember them well.
grammar: よく覚えてるよ — よく here means 'well/clearly.' 〜てる is the contracted progressive — he is still in the state of remembering.

text: ここで休んでいく
translation: We'll rest here for a bit.

vocabulary.meaning: to do something and then go (action done before moving on)

grammar: 〜ていく here means stopping to do something before proceeding — 'rest and then head out.'

text: でもこれアルベド人の店ですよ
translation: But this is an Al Bhed shop, you know.

vocabulary.meaning: Al Bhed (person of the Al Bhed people)

grammar: ですよ adds a gentle informative assertion — 'I'm letting you know.' Wakka is warning the group about the shop's Al Bhed affiliation.

text: 問題でもあるのか
translation: Is there some kind of problem?

vocabulary.meaning: or something (embedded in noun phrase for 'some kind of')

grammar: 問題でもあるのか — でも here is not 'but' but rather an indefinite marker: 'is there any problem or something?' のか is a direct, slightly impatient question.

text: アルベドは教えに従わないし / それにほらルカでは
translation: The Al Bhed don't follow the teachings, and also — well, in Luca…

vocabulary.meaning: to follow, to obey, to comply with

grammar: 〜し at the end of a clause lists reasons in a non-exhaustive way — 'they don't follow the teachings, and…'

text: あいつらユーナをさらったんですよ / ガードがだらしないからだな
translation: Those guys kidnapped Yuna! / That's because the guardian was careless.

vocabulary.meaning: to kidnap, to carry off, to abduct

grammar: 〜からだ is a cause-result structure: 'because of [reason], that happened.' Auron is deflecting Wakka's blame onto the guardians — including himself.

text: アーロンさんはワッカさんの体調を気にして
translation: Auron, worried about Wakka's condition,

vocabulary.meaning: to be concerned about, to worry about

grammar: The sentence is suspended with 〜して — Auron's concern about Wakka leads to the next action (entering the Al Bhed shop). Narrative description.

text: 俺は大丈夫だ / 俺が疲れた
translation: I'm fine. / I'm the one who's tired.

vocabulary.meaning: to get tired, to be exhausted

grammar: 俺が疲れた — the が marks 俺 as the exhausted one (not Wakka), with slight contrast emphasis. Auron admitting he's the one who actually needs the rest.

text: おーすっげー
translation: Whoa, amazing!

vocabulary.meaning: amazing, incredible (rough contraction of すごい)

grammar: すっげー is a rough, excited contraction of すごい — Tidus reacting to the sunset view from the Al Bhed shop.

text: キーリカで見たのとは全然違っていた
translation: It was completely different from what I'd seen at Kilika.

vocabulary.meaning: completely different, not the same at all

grammar: 〜で見たのとは = compared to what I saw at ~. とは marks contrast in comparison. 違っていた — past progressive state of difference.

text: 静かで優しい夕日だった
translation: It was a quiet, gentle sunset.
grammar: 静かで is the て-form of 静かだ, connecting two adjectives — 'quiet and gentle.' Tidus's lyrical internal narration.

text: 何してるっすか
translation: What are you doing?

vocabulary.meaning: what are you doing (casual: 何をしているの)
casual polite question ending (contraction of ですか)

grammar: っすか is characteristic of Wakka's slightly respectful but casual speech register.

text: きれい
translation: Beautiful.
grammar: A single-word utterance — Yuna captivated by the sunset.

text: だよな
translation: It is, isn't it.
grammar: だよな = だよ (assertion) + な (seeking agreement). Tidus casually agreeing.

text: こんな風に / 穏やかな世界でね
translation: Like this — in a peaceful world.
grammar: でね — で (in/at) + ね (soft emphasis, feminine). Yuna trailing off wistfully, setting up the next wish.

text: 毎日、ニコニコして暮らせたらいいのにな
translation: If only we could live every day with smiles on our faces.

vocabulary.meaning: to live, to get by, to spend one's days
if only ~, I wish ~ (expressing unfulfilled wish)

grammar: 〜たらいいのにな is a wish structure: 〜たら (conditional) + いい (good) + のに (regret/wish) + な (reflective). Expresses a wish about a counterfactual state.

text: ユーナがシンを倒せばそうなるんだろ?
translation: That'll happen if Yuna defeats Sin, right?

vocabulary.meaning: to become that way, to turn out like that

grammar: 〜ばそうなる is a standard conditional: 'if [X happens], then [Y].' んだろ is a casual tag seeking confirmation.

text: また、新しいシンが生まれちゃうけどね / そうなったらまた倒せばいいよ
translation: But a new Sin will be born again… / When that happens, we'll just defeat it again.

vocabulary.meaning: end up doing ~ (てしまう contracted)

grammar: そうなったらまた〜ばいいよ = 'when that happens, all we have to do is ~.' 〜ばいいよ is a casual reassurance: 'just do X and it'll be fine.'

text: そう、できたらいいな
translation: Yeah, I hope we can do that.

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to, to manage
I hope ~ happens, it would be nice if ~

grammar: できたらいいな = 'it would be nice if we could.' A gentle, slightly wistful wish — Yuna not quite committing to Tidus's optimistic framing.

text: ユーナならできるって、他の召喚師に負けんなよ
translation: If it's you, Yuna, you can do it — don't lose to the other summoners.

vocabulary.meaning: if it's ~, in the case of ~

grammar: 〜ならできる = 'if it's you, you can.' って is a casual assertive. 負けんなよ = 負けるな + よ in rough speech — 'don't lose!'

text: でも、なんでシンは復活するんだ?
translation: But why does Sin come back?

vocabulary.meaning: to revive, to come back to life, to resurrect

grammar: 〜んだ adds a demand for explanation — Tidus genuinely puzzled and wanting an answer.

text: シンは人間に与えられた罰だから
translation: Because Sin is a punishment given to humanity.

vocabulary.meaning: to give, to bestow, to grant

grammar: 〜に与えられた is passive: 'bestowed upon ~.' 〜だから = 'because ~' — Yuna presenting the Yevonite explanation.

text: 罪が許されるまでシンは消えないの
translation: Until the sin is forgiven, Sin will not disappear.

vocabulary.meaning: to be forgiven, to be pardoned (passive)

grammar: 〜までは〜ない is a pattern: 'until X, Y will not happen.' の at the end (feminine explanatory particle) — Yuna giving a soft but firm explanation.

text: どうしたら罪は許されるんだ?
translation: How can the sin be forgiven?

vocabulary.meaning: how, what should one do (conditional of どうする)

grammar: どうしたら〜 is a conditional question: 'if we do what, then ~?' A genuine question about how to break the cycle.

text: だいたい、罪ってなんすか? / ああ、機械使って楽したことか
translation: Well to begin with, what even is the 'sin'? / Oh, is it using machines to take it easy?

vocabulary.meaning: in the first place, roughly, basically
to take it easy, to make things easy for oneself

grammar: だいたい used here means 'in the first place' — a frustrated preamble questioning the premise. 〜したこと = 'the act of doing ~' (nominalizer こと).

text: ああ、でもそれってそんなに悪いことか?
translation: Oh, but is that really such a bad thing?

vocabulary.meaning: that much, so, to that extent

grammar: それって — って is a casual topic marker. そんなに〜か? — rhetorical question challenging the assumption that it's bad.

text: 変なの
translation: It's weird, isn't it.
grammar: 変なの — Yuna expressing soft, slightly frustrated agreement that the whole situation is strange.

text: 小さな頃から当たり前だと思ってたのに
translation: I thought it was just natural from when I was little, yet…
grammar: 〜と思ってたのに = 'I thought it was ~ but…' のに at the end expresses contradiction between expectation and reality, with a nuance of emotional surprise or resignation.

text: 悪いから悪いと思ってたけど本当は
translation: I thought it was bad just because it was called bad, but actually…
grammar: 悪いから悪いと思ってた = 'I thought it was bad because [they said] it was bad' — a circular reasoning admission. 本当は suspends the sentence before the next line.

text: わからない
translation: I don't know.

vocabulary.meaning: I don't understand, I don't know

grammar: The conclusion of Yuna's honest admission — she doesn't actually know if using machines is truly wrong.

text: 知らないことたくさんあるんだ / それじゃあ、俺と一緒だ
translation: There are a lot of things I don't know. / Then you're just like me.
grammar: 〜んだ adds warmth and personal disclosure. それじゃあ〜と一緒だ = 'in that case, that's the same as ~' — Tidus finding common ground.

text: 評判師がそんなことでは いけませんぞ
translation: A summoner simply cannot be like that.

vocabulary.meaning: here: likely a mishear/subtitle error for 召喚師 (summoner)
in such a state, being like that
must not, cannot, it won't do

grammar: 〜ではいけない = 'it won't do to be like that / that is unacceptable.' ぞ adds a pompous, authoritative flair — this character is putting on airs.

text: 似てた似てた
translation: It was so similar, so similar!
grammar: Reduplication emphasizes the degree of similarity — someone is doing an impression of another character (likely Seymour or Maester Mika) and it was spot-on.

text: ダメだよ どうぞ 失礼なこと / アハハハ
translation: That's awful — stop it — what a rude thing! / Ahahahaha!

vocabulary.meaning: that's no good, you can't do that

grammar: どうぞ here is likely used sarcastically or as a flustered interjection. The fragmented delivery captures a chaotic group laughing scene.

text: あのさ
translation: Hey, listen…

text: 試合中は / 試合のことだけに集中しないとピリッと動けないんだ
translation: During a match — if you don't concentrate only on the match, you can't move sharply.

vocabulary.meaning: during a match, in the middle of a game
sharply, briskly, with a snap (onomatopoeia for alertness)

grammar: 〜しないと〜できない = 'if you don't do X, you can't do Y.' ピリッと is an onomatopoeic adverb — snappy, quick, alert movement.

text: うーん
translation: Hmm…

text: うーん
translation: Hmm…

text: 最前列右から5番目の女の子かわいいとか
translation: Like, 'the girl in the front row, fifth from the right is cute'…
grammar: 〜とか = 'things like ~' (listing with implication of more examples). Tidus is giving examples of distracting thoughts during a match.

text: デートするならどこ行こうとか / 考えてると負けちゃうんだよな
translation: 'If I were to go on a date, where would we go?' — if you think about stuff like that, you lose.

vocabulary.meaning: end up doing (てしまう contracted)

grammar: 考えてると = 考えていると — while/if you're thinking about it. 負けちゃうんだよな = you'll end up losing + emphatic/reflective んだよな.

text: だから、ユーナも先のことは後でゆっくり考えるっすよ
translation: So Yuna, think about the future slowly, later.
grammar: 〜っすよ = casual polite form (です + よ contracted). Wakka giving advice from his blitzball experience.

text: めんどくさいこと考えるのはシーンを倒した後でいいだろ / そうだね
translation: Worrying about troublesome things can wait until after Sin is defeated, right? / Yeah.

vocabulary.meaning: it's fine to do ~ [at some time]

grammar: 〜のは after で marks the time — 'doing X can wait until after Y.' だろ is a casual tag: 'right?'

text: でもさあ あんなでっかいのどうやって倒すんだ
translation: But how do you even beat something that huge?
grammar: でっかい is a colloquial intensified form of 大きい. 〜んだ adds a demanding, genuinely puzzled question tone.

text: 究極召喚
translation: The Final Aeon.

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん

grammar: A single compound noun as a complete answer — Lulu's characteristic economy of words.

text: シンを倒し得る唯一の力 究極召喚
translation: The Final Aeon — the only power capable of defeating Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: capable of defeating, able to defeat (〜得る = potential/possible)

grammar: 〜得る (うる/える) is a literary potential auxiliary: 'capable of doing ~.' 唯一の力 = 'the sole power.' The phrase is restated with extra formality.

text: その力を身につけるのが 私たち召喚士の旅の目的なの / 究極召喚の祈り子様は 北の果てで召喚士を待ってるんだ
translation: Gaining that power is the purpose of our pilgrimage as summoners. / The fayth of the Final Aeon is waiting for summoners at the far north.

vocabulary.meaning: to acquire, to master, to make one's own
fayth (one who has offered their body for a summoning)
the far north, the end of the north

grammar: 〜のが〜なの: 'the thing of doing X is Y' — nominalizer の + が topic + predicate. なの at the end is feminine explanatory.

text: 最果ての地 ザナルカンド
translation: The land at the very end — Zanarkand.

vocabulary.meaning: the farthest end, the uttermost limit, the remotest place

grammar: A noun phrase appositive — 最果ての地 describes Zanarkand. The dramatic pause structure emphasizes its mythic remoteness.

text: 勘違いするな 千年前に滅んだ都市の遺跡だ
translation: Don't misunderstand. It's the ruins of a city that perished a thousand years ago.

vocabulary.meaning: to perish, to be destroyed, to fall

grammar: するな is the blunt negative imperative — 'do not ~.' Auron cutting in to correct any romantic notions Tidus might have about Zanarkand.

text: 本当に遺跡なのか / そう聞いてるけど
translation: Is it really ruins? / That's what I've heard.

vocabulary.meaning: to hear that ~, to have been told so

grammar: 〜けど at the end softens the statement — 'that's what I've heard, but [I'm not sure].' Tidus pressing because he knows his Zanarkand differently.

text: 信用できなければ自分の目で確かめることだ
translation: If you can't trust it, verify it with your own eyes.

vocabulary.meaning: to confirm, to verify, to check

grammar: 〜ことだ as a sentence ending suggests 'the thing to do is ~' — a firm recommendation or mild command. Auron's characteristic 'see for yourself.'

text: ユーナそろそろ中へ入れ
translation: Yuna, it's about time you went inside.
grammar: 入れ is the blunt imperative of 入る. Auron is matter-of-fact — it's getting late or they need to rest.

text: ザナルカンド、一緒に行けるかな?
translation: Zanarkand — will we be able to go together, I wonder?

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to go (potential form of 行く)

grammar: 〜かな as a question directed at another is gentle and hopeful — Yuna asking Tidus if they'll both make it to Zanarkand.

text: うん、行く
translation: Yeah, I'll go.
grammar: A simple, direct affirmation — Tidus's promise to see it through.

text: ザナルカンドへ行って、自分の目で確かめるよ
translation: I'll go to Zanarkand and see it with my own eyes.
grammar: 〜て connects the two verbs sequentially: go and then verify. よ at the end is a confident assertion.

text: それは、俺のザナルカンドじゃない
translation: That — isn't my Zanarkand.
grammar: A wistful internal monologue — Tidus knowing that the ruined Zanarkand they're heading to is not the vibrant city he came from.

text: って、確かめたかった
translation: …is what I wanted to confirm.
grammar: って here quotes his own internal thought from the previous line. 確かめたかった = wanted to verify — a quiet, sad admission of what was driving him.

text: すまないが通行止めだ
translation: I'm sorry, but the road is closed.

vocabulary.meaning: I'm sorry, excuse me (sincere male apology)

grammar: すまないが = 'I apologize, but ~' — a polite way to deliver unwelcome news. 通行止め is a compound noun (通行 'passage' + 止め 'stop').

text: あんたたち召喚士様とガードだろ / 迷惑かけてすまないな
translation: You all are a summoner and guardians, right? / Sorry for the inconvenience.
grammar: 〜だろ is casual confirmation-seeking. すまないな — the な softens the apology into something warm and sincere rather than formal.

text: 協力感謝する
translation: I thank you for your cooperation.
grammar: A terse, formal expression of gratitude — dropping the object marker for concision.

text: またお会いできましたね、ユーナドン
translation: We meet again, Lady Yuna.

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to meet again (humble/polite)

grammar: またお会いできましたね = 'We were able to meet again.' お会いする is the humble form of 会う. ね seeks gentle affirmation. ユーナドン is likely a subtitle rendering of ユーナ殿 (殿 = formal/archaic honorific).

text: どうしましたか?お困りのようですが
translation: What's the matter? You seem to be in some difficulty.
grammar: お困りのようですが = 'it seems you are having difficulty, but ~.' ようだ expresses appearance/inference based on evidence.

text: 実は
translation: The truth is…

vocabulary.meaning: actually, to tell the truth, in fact

grammar: 実は is a classic opener for revealing information — Yuna beginning to explain the problem.

text: なるほど
translation: I see.

vocabulary.meaning: I see, indeed, that makes sense

grammar: なるほど acknowledges understanding — Seymour has heard Yuna's explanation.

text: お待ちしておりました / 作戦司令部にご案内いたします
translation: I have been expecting you. / I will guide you to the command center.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました
ごあんないいたします

grammar: Both phrases use the most formal humble register (〜しておりました, 〜いたします) — an officer receiving Seymour with maximum respect.

text: その前に頼みがある / はっ!何なりと
translation: Before that, I have a request. / Yes sir! Whatever you need.

vocabulary.meaning: anything at all, whatever you wish

grammar: はっ is a military-style interjection of acknowledgment (like 'Yes sir!'). 何なりと = 'please say whatever you like/need' — an open offer to serve.

text: 召喚師ユウナ殿とガードたちも通してほしいのだが
translation: I would like summoner Yuna and her guardians to be allowed through as well.

vocabulary.meaning: to let through, to allow to pass

grammar: 〜のだが is a formal softened request: 'it is that I would like ~ but [can you accommodate it?]' The のだが trails off politely rather than making a direct demand.

text: お言葉ですがシーモア様 / 君に迷惑はかけない
translation: With all due respect, Lord Seymour… / I won't cause you any trouble.

vocabulary.meaning: with all due respect, I beg your pardon but (polite disagreement opener)

grammar: お言葉ですが is a formal way to politely object or express hesitation before disagreeing. 迷惑はかけない = 'will not impose/cause trouble' — the は contrastively marks that trouble specifically won't happen.

text: 責任はすべて私が取る
translation: I will take full responsibility.
grammar: 責任を取る is an idiomatic expression: 'to take responsibility.' すべて emphasizes that all accountability falls on Seymour.

text: かしこまりました通行を許可いたします
translation: Understood. I will grant passage.

vocabulary.meaning: to permit, to allow, to grant

grammar: かしこまりました is the most deferential form of 'understood' — used by subordinates to superiors. 〜いたします is humble speech form.

text: さあどうぞ / ありがとうございます
translation: Please, go ahead. / Thank you very much.

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございます
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございます

text: ユーナ行くわよ
translation: Yuna, we're going.
grammar: わよ is a characteristically feminine assertive ending — Lulu prompting Yuna to move. The combination of わ (feminine) + よ (assertion) is Lulu's speech style.
